en.title: Chris Columbus Didn't Know About Home Alone Reboot Before Criticizing It
en.summary: The director of the beloved Christmas classic Home Alone has voiced strong opinions against any potential reboots, only to learn minutes later that one is already in the works with Macaulay Culkin returning.
en.body:
It’s a tale as old as Hollywood: a beloved classic is revisited, and the original architect is less than thrilled. Such is the case with **Chris Columbus**, the director behind the iconic 1990 film **Home Alone**. Just moments before news broke that **Macaulay Culkin** would reprise his role as Kevin McCallister in a new iteration of the holiday favorite, Columbus shared his firm belief that a **Home Alone** sequel simply *couldn't* work without **Catherine O’Hara**. Speaking to Variety, Columbus stated, 

> "Catherine, as I’ve always said, is 50% of Home Alone. There’s the yin and yang of Home Alone: Catherine O’Hara and Macaulay Culkin. Without those two in the film, there is no film, because they create the emotional epicenter of that film."

He further elaborated that the magic of the original was deeply tied to the dynamic between O'Hara's Kate McCallister and Culkin's Kevin. For Columbus, the emotional core of the film was intrinsically linked to their relationship, making any attempt to recapture that without both actors a non-starter. He even suggested that any such attempts would be "ridiculous."

## A Director's Doubts Meet Studio Reality

Columbus's candid remarks, made without prior knowledge of the impending announcement, paint a picture of an artist protective of his legacy. He's not alone in his skepticism; he previously told Entertainment Tonight that attempting to recreate the magic of **Home Alone** 35 years later is "a mistake." The director has even accused himself of repeating the formula with **Home Alone 2**, questioning its own necessity beyond the laughs. With **Joe Pesci** rarely acting outside of specific projects and **John Heard** having passed away, the original cast's availability is limited, leaving **Daniel Stern** as the most likely returning actor from the original trio of antagonists, though he too has faced recent career setbacks. The new project, reportedly penned and produced by **Seth Rogen** and **Evan Goldberg**, aims to put a new spin on the premise, with Kevin now inadvertently endangering his own children.

## Fan Reaction and Franchise Fatigue

For fans who grew up with Kevin's booby traps and his mother's frantic search, this news is a mixed bag. The idea of **Macaulay Culkin** returning is undeniably appealing, tapping into a powerful wave of nostalgia. However, the director's strong words echo a growing sentiment of franchise fatigue. Audiences are increasingly wary of reboots and legacy sequels that feel like cash grabs rather than genuine creative endeavors. Columbus’s assertion that the original film was a "very special moment" that "can’t really recapture" resonates with many who feel that some films are best left untouched, their iconic status preserved.

## What's Next

Details regarding the full cast and the official release date for the new **Home Alone** project have not yet been announced. Fans will be watching closely to see how this new chapter unfolds and whether it can overcome the original director's reservations.

content_raw: Home Alone director Chris Columbus put a nail through the foot of the Home Alone reboot/legacy sequel/thing minutes before finding out about it. Variety reportedly spoke to Columbus just before it reported on Macaulay Culkin’s return to the red sweater and told the outlet that a Home Alone sequel with Culkin and not Catherine O’Hara, who died earlier this year, wouldn’t work. “Catherine, as I’ve always said, is 50% of Home Alone ,” Columbus says. “There’s the yin and yang of Home Alone : Catherine O’Hara and Macaulay Culkin. Without those two in the film, there is no film, because they create the emotional epicenter of that film.” He continues, “It was really about Catherine and Macaulay. If anyone ever wanted to do a sequel, unfortunately that can’t happen.”  Earlier today, news broke that Culkin had signed on to reprise cinema’s most famous abandoned child and home security expert in a new Home Alone movie, in which Kevin endangers his children for a change. The movie will reportedly be written and produced by Seth Rogen and Evan Goldberg. The rest of the cast’s participation is still unknown. John Heard died in 2017, and Joe Pesci rarely acts for anyone other than Martin Scorsese and Pete Davidson , so that really leaves Daniel Stern, who was fired from an ABC sitcom by Home Alone  rights holders Disney earlier this year . Without them, Columbus doesn’t hold out much hope for success. “I think you potentially could still entertain the idea of doing another Home Alone with the cast,” Columbus explains. “Not any of these ridiculous follow-ups to the first. And I only say ridiculous because it’s weird with filmmakers. They don’t understand why that cast works so well. It’s always about the cast. It’s like The Goonies . It’s about the cast.” Nevertheless, he did say he hoped to work with Culkin “on something” again. “Maybe it’ll be Home Alone -related, maybe it won’t.” It sounds like he’s saying he’d be willing to make the movie if asked, but also that it wouldn’t work because O’Hara is no longer with us. But this is also the man who’s making a new Gremlins without Joe Dante because he didn’t like what Dante did with Gremlins 2: The New Batch .
